workerReply:
Slice 2 is done and committed on `stage-5-live-service`, and the plan in `.agenthub/handoff.md` now includes the day-trading change. The full test suite passes (105 tests).

**What was built**
- **Market calendar** (`live/calendar.py`): NYSE holidays worked out from rules, including Good Friday, Juneteenth from 2022 and how holidays on weekends are moved. It also covers one-off closures, extra holidays you can add in the config, 13:00 early closes, and session times in America/New_York, so daylight-saving changes are handled.
- **Strategies** (`live/strategies.py`): a strategy says when it wants to decide and what it wants to hold. The current one is the deployed daily model with 5-day smoothing. Its decision is due 30 minutes after the close and expires at the next open, so a daemon that was down overnight never trades a stale signal. Market data is re-downloaded every cycle into one cache file per symbol, so the cache doesn't grow every day.
- **Daemon** (`live/service.py`). Each cycle:
  1. reconciles with the broker;
  2. refreshes data and gets the targets;
  3. checks for stale data;
  4. records equity and runs the drawdown breaker;
  5. sends orders through the safety layer;
  6. reconciles again and marks the cycle done.
  - A cycle that fails (network, stale data, kill switch, halt) is retried every 5 minutes until it expires, then marked skipped. A finished cycle never runs again, so restarts are safe.
  - SIGTERM and SIGINT stop the loop cleanly after the current cycle. A lock file stops two daemons trading the same account.
  - It uses only pathlib and cross-platform calls; on Linux the lock uses `fcntl`.
- **`serve` command** with `--once`, `--status`, `--dry-run` and `--clear-halt`, plus `configs/live.json`. The simulated broker stays the default. A real account needs only config and environment-variable changes.
  - `--clear-halt` also resets the drawdown peak; otherwise the breaker would trip again on the next cycle.

**What I verified**
- 21 new tests: calendar for 2026 and edge years, run-once-per-day and restart idempotency, stale-data retry, cycle expiry, kill switch, drawdown halt then clearing it, a crash after sending orders (no duplicates), dry-run, position drift, clean stop on SIGTERM/SIGINT, the lock, building from config, and the CLI.
- A real run on live Yahoo data at 06:46 ET today with the deployed model, using throwaway state files: `serve --status` showed the 2026-11-04 cycle as due, and `serve --once --dry-run` produced 20 signals and 16 orders, with nothing sent.

**Decisions I made**
- **Ubuntu deployment:** the old plan said Windows Task Scheduler; it now uses systemd.
- **Intraday before the dashboard:** the live stream only makes sense at intraday speed, since a daily bot produces one event a day.
- **Free intraday data exists after all:** yfinance has 60 days of 5-minute bars, and Alpaca's free feed has years of minute bars but needs the free paper keys. 60 days is too little to train PPO, so training will need the Alpaca keys. I corrected the handoff note that said intraday data wasn't free.
- **Halts block exits:** for the daily strategy, a halt or the kill switch blocks every order, including sells. The intraday slice will allow flatten-at-close orders during a halt.

**Revised plan**
- Slice 3 is the day-trading strategy:
  - 5-minute bars and intraday features;
  - momentum/opening-range and mean-reversion baselines first, then PPO, tested walk-forward by month;
  - forced flat before the close;
  - high-risk sizing from short to 2x leverage;
  - new safety rules: leverage cap, daily loss limit, short-selling switch, and a $25k pattern-day-trader guard;
  - the daemon will decide every 5 minutes.
- Then slice 4, a live dashboard streaming orders, positions and equity; slice 5, replay of past sessions so Daniel can watch it trade; slice 6, systemd deployment.
- The handoff notes that most retail intraday strategies don't survive trading costs, and that leverage multiplies losses as well as gains.

`main` is unchanged because Stage 5 isn't finished, and `[COMPLETED]` is not set. Next is slice 3.

workerReply:
Slice 3 is built, tested and committed on `stage-5-live-service`, but no day-trading strategy made money out-of-sample after costs. All 127 tests pass.

**How it was tested:** Yahoo 5-minute bars for 18 liquid stocks and ETFs, 60 sessions (2026-08-12 to 2026-11-04). The first 40 sessions were used to build and tune; the last 20 were looked at once. Costs are 2 bp per fill (4 bp round trip), and positions are closed 10 minutes before the close.

| Strategy (results on the 20 test sessions) | After costs | Before costs | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| VWAP mean reversion, best settings on the first 40 | −2.2% | −1.0% | Best before the test; failed on it, loses even before costs |
| Same, 2x leverage | −4.4% | | Leverage only doubles the loss |
| Same, costs doubled | −3.4% | | |
| Same, long only | −2.9% | | |
| Momentum | −2.3% to −3.4% | | Pays about 12–18 bp a day in costs |
| Opening-range breakout | −0.1% to +0.4% | | The +0.4% (t 0.26) is noise, and the version that lost on the first 40 sessions would never have been picked |
| PPO (3 seeds) | −0.67% | −0.06% | Mostly learned to trade little; no edge before costs |

- **Shuffle check:** with the bar order randomised inside each day, the picked strategy loses about the same (−23%/yr vs −24%/yr). It found no real intraday pattern.
- **Sample size:** 20 sessions is too few to tell skill from luck either way. The bot should not get real money until a strategy passes this same test on years of data (Alpaca history, or months of bars the daemon builds up itself).
- **Bug fixed:** a test caught a look-ahead leak (the first bar of each day used a volatility figure computed over the whole period). I fixed it and reran everything; the baseline numbers came out the same.

**What was built**
- **Data:**
  - Yahoo 5-minute bars, merged into one file per symbol on every download, so history grows past Yahoo's 60-day limit while the daemon runs.
  - An optional Alpaca loader for years of history. It is tested against a fake server but not run, since there are no keys here.
  - A synthetic intraday generator with planted momentum or mean reversion, for tests.
- **Backtester:** decides at a bar's close and fills at the next bar's open, paying spread and slippage. It supports shorts and leverage and always ends the day flat. The live daemon replays the same logic, and a test checks that it makes the same decisions.
- **Safety additions:**
  - leverage cap;
  - short-selling switch;
  - daily loss limit (closes everything and blocks new trades until the next day);
  - pattern-day-trader guard ($25k minimum, exits only below it);
  - forced flat before the close;
  - a cap on orders per cycle.
  - A halt now still lets positions be closed. The kill switch still freezes everything, including closing positions; to flatten in an emergency, trigger a halt instead.
- **Simulated broker:** now supports margin and shorting.
- **Daemon:** runs every 5 minutes: 76 decisions a day (40 on early-close days), the last one closes everything, and a restart never re-sends orders. A full replay of the real 2026-11-04 session finished all 76 cycles with 52 orders, ended flat, and took about 3 s per cycle for 18 symbols.
- **Commands and configs:** `intraday-download`, `intraday-research [--ppo]`, `configs/intraday.json`, and `configs/live_intraday.json` (sandbox day trader, 2x leverage, shorts on, 3% daily loss limit). That config runs the VWAP strategy only so the dashboard has something to show. It is not evidence the strategy works.

**Decisions I made:** Yahoo's 60 days instead of blocking on Alpaca keys; 2 bp per fill with no commission (as on Alpaca), and no margin interest because nothing is held overnight; the PDT minimum is configurable, so check the current FINRA rule before any real-money use.

The handoff has the full results tables and updated "How to run" / "How to test" sections, and the full report is `reports/intraday/yahoo_60d.md`. `main` is unchanged and `[COMPLETED]` is not set. Next is slice 4, the live dashboard streaming orders, positions and equity, then replay and Ubuntu deployment.

After that, for the move to a real broker, add a short "go-live checklist" documenting the three live gates and the requirement for a longer-history validation first.
